questions.question: When backing up, a helper:

options.text: Should be used whenever possible.
Often adds to the confusion of backing.
Should only be used if the driver is not feeling confident.
Would likely get in the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper whenever you can to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving:

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
The engine should be turned off.
The check can be done from inside the vehicle.
The check can be done by looking at a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: To check your lights before driving, turn off the engine and set the parking brake. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle and look at each light to make sure it works.

questions.question: If a car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Drive on the shoulder.
Pull off the roadway.
Drive faster.
Allow the vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you, let it pass. Create more space in front of your vehicle so you can avoid sudden stops. This prevents rear-end crashes and makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Driving impaired.
Inappropriately dressed.
Using the heat inside their vehicle.
Enjoying the fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick can cause crashes. An open window in cold weather may indicate a driver is impaired.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before beginning the hill
After you have already started the hill
As far down the hill as possible
At the bottom of the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before beginning the hill
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you start going down a hill. This helps you control your speed without using your brakes too much.

questions.question: If you face an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
React to the driver's gestures.
Challenge the driver to a road race.
Ignore the driver, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, stay away from them if you can. Do not challenge them or make eye contact. Do not react to rude gestures.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:

options.text: At least one-half.
About one-third.
About one-quarter.
About one-eighth.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one-half.
questions.explanation: On packed snow, cut your speed in half or more. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop or turn. You must drive slower to stay safe.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Never be used.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers when you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off once your bus has completely cleared the tracks.

questions.question: During a bus ride:

options.text: Carry-on bags may be kept in the aisle.
Passengers may sit in the aisle.
Aisles must remain free of obstacles.
Items may be placed in the aisle if passengers could step over them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Aisles must remain free of obstacles.
questions.explanation: Keep aisles clear of all bags and items. Nothing should be in the aisle that could make passengers trip. Store baggage safely to prevent damage.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection:

options.text: Should never be completed the same way two times in a row.
Should always be completed in the same order.
Should only be done if it is sunny outside.
Should not be done if the driver thinks the vehicle is in good condition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be completed in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. Following the same steps will help you remember all the checks and make sure you do not miss anything.

questions.question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, which statement is true?

options.text: You do not need to identify the ABS.
You do not need to check the windshield wipers.
You only need to check shock absorbers on one axle.
You must check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external inspection of the pre-trip test, check that the steering box is secure and not leaking.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may mean the driver:

options.text: Is impaired.
Is colorblind.
Does not know traffic rules.
Is very patient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have consumed alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is a warning sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: Small amounts of hazardous material can be transported on a bus if:

options.text: The driver receives extra pay.
There is no other way to transport it.
Passengers are told in advance.
Bad weather is not in the forecast.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no other way to transport it.
questions.explanation: Small amounts of hazardous materials may be carried on a bus only if no other transportation method exists. However, some hazardous materials cannot be carried on a bus under any circumstances.

questions.question: If you must write a vehicle inspection report, when must you sign it?

options.text: Every day.
Only if defects were found and repaired or verified as not needing repair.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repaired or verified as not needing repair.
questions.explanation: Sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and certified as repaired or not needing repair.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for one of two reasons. Which is one of them?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure.
You are driving uphill.
The brakes get too cold.
The brakes are used too much in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of hydraulic pressure.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failures happen for two main reasons. The first is brake fade from overuse on downhill grades. The second is loss of hydraulic pressure in the brake system. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to reduce driving distractions?

options.text: Pre-program radio stations.
Plan your route before driving.
Eat while driving.
Adjust mirrors before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eat while driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road would make you carsick.
Part of the vehicle gives you a point of reference.
It is illegal to show only the road.
You need to see reflections of nearby vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of the vehicle gives you a point of reference.
questions.explanation: Include part of your vehicle in your mirrors. This helps you judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: If using a helper while backing your vehicle, where should they stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger side.
In front of the driver side.
On the side of the truck.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Agree on hand signals before backing, especially a clear signal to stop.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the flames.
Aim at the ground about two feet from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the fire as you can. Aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire, not the top.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Stay in their path.
Make eye contact with them.
Make gestures at them.
Report them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Report them.
questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report the driver to authorities when it is safe to do so.
